thread:
lena_support: FYI customer Paul (org 12345) opened a ticket — p95/p99 on /v1/generate jumped at ~09:10 UTC. They see 5-8s p95 and p99 spikes to 15-25s, plus some 429s and 504s. ticket: https://support.example/t/54321

ops-bot: ALERT: ingress-backlog: ingress-queue length > 500 (10m avg) — service=ingress-gateway region=us-west1

omar_oncall: Oncall — looking now. Is the traffic only in us-west1 and limited to org 12345? Any recent deploys?

lena_support: Customer says it's us-west1 and only their org. No deploys reported on their side. Paul, can you paste a minimal repro request?

paul_customer: here's a minimal curl we run from our side (we hit the same rate pattern repeatedly):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"summarize: ..."}'
```
Response sample: 200 usually, but some calls return 504 and a few 429s. IDs: r:aa12, r:aa13, r:aa14

sri_eng_runtime: I'm seeing corresponding metrics — admission control is thrashing. worker_pool=decoder-1 in us-west1 showing concurrency ~410 while configured limit was 400, queue_len ~620, p95 tokens latency ~6.8s, p99 ~18.9s. Many requests sat in the admit queue. Also seeing an internal batch job fanout spike at 09:08 that correlates.

kai_sre: Sounds like overloaded workers + admission window exhaustion. Short-term mitigations: reduce per-tenant concurrency for org 12345 to 200, enable fallback routing to a smaller model variant (redwood-3b-quant) for best-effort traffic, and temporarily raise admit-reject threshold to shed noisy fanout. Longer-term: add per-tenant queue-length alerts + backpressure metrics.

omar_oncall: I'll patch the tenant limit and route policy now. Patch commands:
```
# patch tenant concurrency limit
redwoodctl tenants patch 12345 --set concurrency_limit=200 --region us-west1
# enable fallback route for heavy requests
redwoodctl routing add-fallback --tenant 12345 --from redwood-13b --to redwood-3b-quant --priority best-effort
```

ops-bot: config-change: tenant 12345 concurrency_limit updated 400 -> 200 by omar_oncall at 2024-08-17T09:17:05Z

omar_oncall: routing rule applied, fallback enabled. Monitoring for immediate impact.

paul_customer: updating — I'm seeing drops in latency already. p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~1.2s. No 504s in the last 30s. Thanks.

sri_eng_runtime: Good — metrics show queue_len down to ~80, decoder concurrency ~190. Admission rejects decreased.

kai_sre: Recommend we also throttle the internal batch job that caused the fanout and add a rate limiter on their job ID. Maya/product owns the outbound batch behavior? @maya_product can you coordinate?

maya_product: Will follow up with the team that owns the batch job. We'll add a client-side exponential backoff and staggered fanout over the next day.

lena_support: I'll update the customer and leave the ticket open until we confirm stability for 24h. Owners: infra (sri_eng_runtime) to add tenant-level queue metrics and an alert; platform (omar_oncall/kai_sre) to draft a safe auto-fallthrough policy; product (maya_product) to fix the batch fanout.

paul_customer: Appreciate the quick response — we'll hold off big jobs until you confirm the fix.

omar_oncall: Noting follow-ups and action items. Closing immediate escalation — will keep monitoring.

ops-bot: monitor-note: follow-up alerts created — alert:tenant-queue-high (threshold 200) assigned to sri_eng_runtime, severity=P2

lena_support: closing thread in Slack, keeping ticket open in support.
